title: fix(plugin-grid,plugin-gantt,plugin-charts,plugin-view,app-shell): grid, gantt and chart refetch in place on the invalidation bus; no view is remounted to show a write (objectui#10035)
body:
Fixes #10035
Clause-②: no — renderers refetch in place instead of remounting. No schema, export or accept set moves.

The remainder of objectui#10035, after objectui#10378 (`Part of #10035`, merged `8e49a9981`). Governing text: AGENTS.md §5 commandment #8's corollary, "refresh data, don't rebuild UI — after a save/action, invalidate the affected data (`notifyDataChanged` from `@object-ui/react`) so consumers refetch in place; never bump a `key=` to remount a subtree". Dispatched by the `domain:ui` seat 2 PM, session `session_014mXUNuFomfj24w7s1pZzhN` (`mode:subagent`, so that id is also this run's).

## What this changes

The three renderers that read no refresh input now read the data-invalidation bus, so neither `ObjectView` layer remounts anything to show a write.

- `@object-ui/plugin-grid` `ObjectGrid`: the load effect names `useDataInvalidation(objectName)`'s nonce and re-reads into the same table (the `RefreshIndicator` path, not the skeleton). Not subscribed when a host hands the rows down (`data`, `bind`, inline `value`). Only the fetch effect region and the import line are touched; the page-size region objectui#10278 edits is not.
- `@object-ui/plugin-gantt` `ObjectGantt`: a nonce move triggers `reload({ silent: true })`, the path the toolbar refresh and every write-readback already use, so `GanttView` stays mounted (scroll, collapsed groups, zoom). The main fetch effect's reload flips `loading` and swaps `GanttView` for the placeholder, which is a remount one level down, so the bus does not go through it. Each nonce is answered once; one that lands while the object-schema gate is closed is dropped, because the gated first load reads rows written before it.
- `@object-ui/plugin-charts` `ObjectChart`: the fetch effect names the nonce, on both binding shapes. Object-bound (`aggregate` / `find`) keys on `schema.objectName`. Dataset-bound (`queryDataset`) keys on the dataset's base object as the query answer names it (`object`, the field the dashboard `DatasetWidget` reads for drill-through), because a dataset node carries no `objectName`.
- `@object-ui/plugin-view` `ObjectView`: `REMOUNT_TO_REFRESH_VIEW_TYPES` and the grid's `remountKey` are gone; every view is keyed on its identity. The sites that move `refreshKey` also notify the bus: the host's own form save and delete (`announceOwnWrite`), and each `onMutation` write it hears (republished with the event's `recordId`).
- `@object-ui/app-shell` `ObjectView`: `REMOUNT_TO_REFRESH_VISUALIZATIONS`, the whitelist scan and the chart branch's `remountKey` are gone; `ListView` and both chart branches are keyed on identity. The bump sites that change DATA without a data-source write now go through `refreshData` (counter plus `notifyDataChanged`): the action runtime's refresh (server, api and flow actions), `useObjectActions`' refresh (delete, the `refresh` action), realtime events, and import completion. View CRUD keeps bumping the counter alone: it changes view metadata, which reaches every renderer as props.
- `.changeset/10035-renderers-read-invalidation.md` (`patch` on the five packages). The pending `.changeset/10035-objectview-refresh-in-place.md` from the first half is corrected in prose only (frontmatter untouched): its closing paragraph said gantt, chart and standalone-grid views "are still remounted after a write", which this change makes false before it could publish.

## Measurement (dispatch zone 2)

- H1 confirmed on BASE `ab50ccc12`: both remount sets and the grid `remountKey` present (`REMOUNT_TO_REFRESH_VIEW_TYPES` 4 occurrences, `REMOUNT_TO_REFRESH_VISUALIZATIONS` 3; `useDataInvalidation` 0 in all three renderer files).
- H2(a): a data-source write reaches the bus only through `useMutationInvalidationBridge`, which the console mounts once in `AppContent`; nothing else bridges. So the bus hears a data-source write in the console, and hears nothing in an embed that does not mount the bridge.
- H2(b), which bump sites stop reaching the renderer once the key stops carrying the counter:
  - plugin-view: all three (`handleFormSuccess`, the delete's `onRefresh`, the `onMutation` subscription) are data-source writes, so they reach the bus through the bridge in the console and never outside it. All three now notify it themselves.
  - app-shell: realtime (no local write at all), import (`importRecords` emits no `onMutation`, read in `data-objectstack`), the action runtime (raw HTTP), and the `refresh` action (no write) would stop. The delete through `useObjectActions` reaches the bus through the bridge anyway, and now also notifies. `externalRefreshKey` needs nothing: `AppContent` bumps it for a form save (a data-source write, which the bridge announces) and for undo / redo (which already call `notifyDataChanged`). View CRUD is metadata.
- H3: the kept-remount pins flipped (below), both sets removed with their comments.
- H4: both chart paths refetch, one pin each.
- H5: one invalidation causes one refetch per renderer. Every in-place pin asserts the delta is exactly 1 (renderer pins: `find` / `aggregate` / `queryDataset` calls; host pins: the self-fetching view's own query).

Why the bus, not a host counter prop or a per-renderer `onMutation` subscription: a prop is one more relay per host (and per renderer), the silent-gap class objectui#7559's relay census exists for, and an `onMutation` subscription misses every change that is not a data-source write (realtime, import, server actions).

## Pins: red on base, green on head

Reverse run, all five source files checked out at BASE `ab50ccc12` with the head pins kept (on-disk blob == base blob for all five; restore proven by `git diff HEAD` empty, status clean, blob == HEAD): `Test Files 5 failed (5)`, `Tests 12 failed | 15 passed (27)`. Every failing in-place case failed on the half the defect predicts:

| pin file | cases red on base | half |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `ObjectGrid.invalidationRefetch-10035.test.tsx` (new) | object-scoped, record-scoped | (b) rows never re-read |
| `ObjectGantt.invalidationRefetch-10035.test.tsx` (new) | in-place refetch | (b) "expected '1' to be '2'" |
| `ObjectChart.invalidationRefetch-10035.test.tsx` (new) | object-bound, dataset-bound | (b) never re-ran its query |
| plugin-view `ObjectView.refreshInPlace-10035.test.tsx` (flipped) | gantt, chart, grid, grid delete | (a) remounted ("expected '4' to be '2'", "expected '2' to be '1'") |
| app-shell `ObjectView.refreshInPlace-10035.test.tsx` (flipped) | whitelist offering gantt and chart, gantt console write, gantt realtime | (a) list remounted; the console-write case trips (b) first: 2 gantt queries, one from the remount and one from the bus |

The negative cases (another object, host rows, inline rows) and the six data-fed plugin-view cases stay green on base, as they should. The gantt file was reworked after that run; its reverse was re-run on the final head: red on (b), restore proven (blob == HEAD).

Report-only: `check-changeset-overwrite` reports the pending 10035 changeset correction (its case 2); `check:changeset-claims` lists 16 pending changesets naming touched files, and none makes a claim about refresh, remount, keys or invalidation (each body scanned).

## Acceptance notes

- `ListView` draws its loading skeleton in place of the visualization while it refetches an empty list (`loading && data.length === 0`), so a gantt or chart there is unmounted and remounted by the list's own refetch when the list has no rows. With no rows the gantt draws nothing either, so no state is lost in practice. `ListView.tsx` is outside this claim (objectui#10327 is in flight on it).
- A dataset-bound chart follows its base object only. A write to an object the dataset joins does not refresh it, the same object granularity every bus reader has. If the query answer names no `object`, the chart has no object to follow and refreshes on its own inputs only. The in-tree adapter passes the field through from the server envelope.
- With the console bridge mounted, a plugin-view `onMutation` write reaches the bus twice in one synchronous dispatch (the bridge, then the host), and React batches them into one render. A form save may then be announced a second time by `announceOwnWrite` after the save resolves. That is at most the two refetches the two key bumps it replaces cost, since each remount fetched.
- No docs page or README describes these components' refresh behaviour, so none became false. commandment #2's docs half has nothing to correct here.
- Embeds that mount the renderers without the console bridge get the bus only from the hosts' own declarations. `object-view` covers its own writes and republishes `onMutation`.

## Deviations

- File surface: the pending `.changeset/10035-objectview-refresh-in-place.md` from the first half is corrected (prose only), as above. It is not in the claim's surface. Leaving it would have published a false paragraph.
- Hosts, not only renderers: app-shell's `refreshData` wraps the bump sites named in H2(b). The ablations show which pins depend on each.
